questions.q: What actually locks an application to one cloud's AI platform over time?
options: The provider's SDK import, endpoint, and credential shape being copied into every file that calls a model
Azure refusing to let apps run on any other cloud's infrastructure
The programming language the application is written in
Nothing — cloud AI platforms cannot create lock-in by design
questions.explain: Lock-in grows from provider-specific SDK calls, endpoints, and credentials scattered throughout a codebase rather than isolated in one place.

questions.q: What does wrapping model calls in a single function like `ask_model()` actually buy you?
options: Faster model inference times
A single seam to change when swapping providers, instead of hunting down every call site across the codebase
Automatic translation between every cloud's billing system
It removes the need for any API key at all
questions.explain: A single wrapper function isolates provider-specific logic, so a future provider swap means changing one function instead of every call site.

questions.q: Why should prompts be kept in files or a prompt store rather than inline in SDK calls?
options: Inline prompts run slower than file-based prompts
So prompts aren't tied to one provider's specific call shape, making them easier to reuse across a swap
Azure requires prompts to be stored in Key Vault
File-based prompts are required for AI Search indexing
questions.explain: Keeping prompts outside inline SDK calls decouples them from any one provider's request format, making a provider swap simpler.

questions.q: Why does the lesson call out noting an embedding's dimension and distance metric explicitly?
options: Because not every provider's embedding model agrees on either one, and a silent mismatch breaks retrieval in a hard-to-debug way
Because dimension and distance metric affect billing directly
Because Azure AI Search requires a specific embedding dimension for all models
Because embeddings without a noted dimension are rejected by every cloud
questions.explain: Embedding dimension and distance metric vary by provider/model — an unnoted mismatch during a swap can silently degrade retrieval quality.

questions.q: What is this lesson's actual recommendation — build a full abstraction layer, or something narrower?
options: Build an elaborate abstraction layer immediately, regardless of whether a migration is ever likely
Ignore portability entirely until a migration is actually announced
A handful of cheap habits — a wrapper function, externalized config and prompts — that don't make a possible future migration harder
Rewrite the entire application in a cloud-agnostic language
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly avoids recommending a heavy abstraction layer, favoring cheap, low-cost habits that keep a future migration from being harder than necessary.
